hero.headline: Indian River County Sheriff's Office seeking information in two death investigations near Sebastian
hero.teaser: The sheriff's office is asking anyone with information about either of the two deaths discovered this week near Sebastian to come forward.
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office is investigating two deaths near Sebastian this week, with authorities seeking information from the public while awaiting toxicology results to determine the causes of death.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said the first body, identified as 44-year-old James Thompson of Brevard County, was found Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line by someone fishing in the area. Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a Sebastian hotel and was last seen Sunday around 1:30 p.m. walking northbound on Highway 1. According to Flowers, Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues, and had purchased methamphetamine on July 3 before entering a manic state. The autopsy showed only a minor contusion on his eyebrow with no signs of violence. The second body, a heavily decomposed 65-year-old man, was discovered Wednesday afternoon in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just across the street from Monday's location. The man had a temporary address with his brother in Sebastian and was out on pretrial release following an arrest by Plantation police on an aggravated battery charge. Flowers said the man had a serious history of seizures and had been taken to a hospital by his brother on Sunday but walked away against medical advice. Plantation police had obtained or were obtaining a warrant for him for absconding on his pretrial release.

Flowers emphasized that at this point nothing connects the two cases, and autopsies revealed no stab wounds or evidence of violence in either death. However, he said both cases remain suspicious and investigations are active. "Any death that isn't a natural death is suspicious. We're always going to look into them and take them seriously," Flowers said. He also warned that the deaths could be related to bad drugs circulating in the area, urging drug users to seek treatment. "If there's something deeper to this and we've got drug-related issues, we want to find out who sold them drugs," Flowers said.

Anyone with information about either case is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous. The sheriff's office will continue investigating both deaths while waiting for toxicology results to determine the exact causes of death.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Martin County shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
cards.body:
A new Aldi opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County residents more affordable grocery options as food prices continue to strain family budgets. Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have an affordable option close to their home. "We're thrilled to have it here," Cheryl said. "Now we have something with reasonable prices that's close by." She said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "We're the type of people who never used to look at prices," Cheryl said. "I will go with what's on sale instead of just with what we want, and we never used to do that."

The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated; they're not gonna go down. It's just I'd be willing to bet on that," they said. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial, because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase and stuff," they said.

The new store provides another shopping option for residents dealing with rising costs at the grocery store. WPTV has been reporting on the issue as prices continue to put pressure on family budgets throughout the area. The discount grocery chain is known for offering lower prices compared to traditional supermarkets, which shoppers say makes a meaningful difference when managing household expenses.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff at Wimbledon to reach final
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 victory Thursday that concluded with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
cards.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who was champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who was champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks as 67th most stressed city in the U.S., financial pressure cited
hero.teaser: A new WalletHub study released this month identifies Port St. Lucie as the 67th most stressed city in America, with financial stress ranking 42nd worst nationwide.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie ranks as the 67th most stressed city in the United States in a study released this month by WalletHub. The report cited that the city is the 42nd most financially stressed in America. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

Compared to other states, Florida performed fairly well, with no cities in the top 35. Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, topping out at 37th in the U.S. In South Florida, Miami was on the list at 50th, with affordable housing being fourth worst in the U.S., and Fort Lauderdale at 83rd. The most stressed cities in the country were Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said some stress is out of our control, due to issues with family, friends or employers. However, where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are. Cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. Lupo added that when moving, it's important to consider how a certain city may impact your mental health, not just your financial opportunities. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

Cities with the least stress included Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, which topped the list of least stressed cities. Fremont is a notably affluent area with average home prices of about $1.5 million. That was followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota.

hero.headline: Park Vista Cobras football team eyes state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
hero.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find their footing early in 2025 but finished strong, winning four of their last five games.

Senior Harris Bender said the team felt good throughout the second half of the 2025 season. He said the Cobras are working to carry that performance through the entire 2026 season and have all the pieces in place now. It is just about executing, he added. Senior Erik Lee said coming in, he feels like the team has the guys needed to get it done, but they also have to put in the work to get there as well.

The ultimate goal for Park Vista is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017. Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said the team has to take it one game at a time and cannot look past anyone. He said the Cobras have to handle business weekly, and if they do that and do their job, that will get them into the playoffs.

Senior Justice Jones said it is going to feel amazing because he already knows it is going to happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League released the nicknames and logos of its four teams on Wednesday, with each team name inspired by pioneering women.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The other teams are the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

cards.headline: Hammerheads Cruise Past St. Lucie Mets 15-3
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter s
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter scored in each of its final seven innings at the plate, steadily pulling away after the Mets grabbed an early lead.

Antonio Jimenez put St. Lucie ahead 2-1 with a two-run homer in the third inning, his second home run in the last three games and his fifth of the season with the Mets. The lead did not last. Jupiter answered with four runs in the bottom of the third to go up 5-2, keyed by a two-run single from Max Williams and an RBI double from Nixon Chirinos.

Jackson Hauge trimmed the deficit to 5-3 with a two-out RBI single in the fourth, but that was the last Mets hit until Elian Peña singled with one out in the eighth. In between, Jupiter reliever Elier Morillo retired all 10 batters he faced, striking out seven.

The Hammerheads kept adding on, scoring two in the fourth, two in the fifth and four in the sixth, the last punctuated by a three-run homer from Chirinos off Caden Wooster.

All nine Jupiter starters reached base and eight collected hits. Leadoff man Luis Cova went 4 for 5, a triple shy of the cycle, while Williams finished 2 for 5 with a homer, three RBI and three runs. For St. Lucie, Peña, Branny De Oleo and Francisco Toledo each went 2 for 4.

Mets starter Christian Rodriguez took the loss, charged with five runs on eight hits over three innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out five.

The Mets (4-12, 37-45) and Hammerheads (7-11, 44-40) continue their series Friday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Barnes shot and killed, family member arrested
cards.teaser: Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children.

His family released a statement asking people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online as the investigation continues, calling his death a senseless act of violence and a deeply painful circumstance that impacts many people. Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as a pillar of the community and a father figure to students who didn't grow up with dads. Coleman, now 37 years old, said Barnes made a life-long impact and maintained communication with former students for decades, well before social media came around. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.
